headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill shifts the financial burden of new grid infrastructure from residential ratepayers to large energy consumers, primarily data centers, by requiring them to pay for their own capacity and collateral.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, consumer advocates, environmental advocates, State Corporation Commission (SCC)
news_headline: Virginia Now Makes Data Centers Post $1.5 Million A Megawatt
news_summary: Virginia's utility regulator approved a new tariff requiring data centers drawing 25 megawatts or more to sign 14-year contracts, pay for capacity, and post $1.5 million collateral per megawatt. These rules, effective January 1, 2027, aim to prevent residential ratepayers from covering stranded costs if data center projects fail or leave.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates public reporting of data center water usage, increasing transparency and enabling better water resource management in Virginia.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental advocates, Potomac Conservancy, Senator Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective July 1, 2026, mandates that data centers' water usage be publicly reported by local utilities on an accessible website. This aims to provide transparency regarding the significant water consumption by data centers, especially in regions facing drought conditions.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill empowers local governments to regulate data center locations and noise levels, addressing community concerns about quality of life and environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents, environmental groups (e.g., Piedmont Environmental Council)
news_headline: Loudoun County houses nearly half of Virginia's data center backup generators
news_summary: Loudoun County, a hub for data centers, faces significant noise complaints and calls for stricter oversight due to thousands of backup generators. Local governments are increasingly taking action to regulate data center siting and noise, reflecting growing community tensions over their environmental and quality-of-life impacts.
